lines.en: Mia, guess what? My landlord lowered the rent, which was a complete surprise.
lines.pt: Mia, adivinha? Meu senhorio baixou o aluguel, o que foi uma surpresa total.

lines.en: Really? That is great news, which probably means he wants you to stay another year.
lines.pt: Sério? Que ótima notícia, o que provavelmente significa que ele quer que você fique mais um ano.

lines.en: Maybe. I also found out that my neighbour is leaving, which makes the building much quieter.
lines.pt: Talvez. Também descobri que meu vizinho vai embora, o que deixa o prédio muito mais silencioso.

lines.en: Lucky you! Mine plays the drums every night, which drives me mad, and he refuses to stop.
lines.pt: Que sorte! O meu toca bateria toda noite, o que me deixa louca, e ele se recusa a parar.

lines.en: Have you talked to him? He might not realise how loud he is, which happens more often than you think.
lines.pt: Você falou com ele? Ele pode não perceber como é barulhento, o que acontece mais do que se imagina.

lines.en: I did, twice. He apologised, which was nice, but he carried on, which was really annoying.
lines.pt: Falei, duas vezes. Ele pediu desculpas, o que foi legal, mas continuou, o que foi muito irritante.

lines.en: Then try the housing office. They told me they take complaints seriously, which I did not expect.
lines.pt: Então tente o setor de moradia. Disseram que levam as reclamações a sério, o que eu não esperava.

lines.en: Good idea. Last week I missed the bus and the train, which meant I arrived two hours late.
lines.pt: Boa ideia. Semana passada perdi o ônibus e o trem, o que significou chegar duas horas atrasada.

lines.en: Oh no. And your boss, who is usually strict, said nothing, which is almost unbelievable.
lines.pt: Poxa. E seu chefe, que costuma ser rígido, não disse nada, o que é quase inacreditável.

lines.en: I know! He was in a good mood because Ireland won on Saturday, which made everybody happy.
lines.pt: Eu sei! Ele estava de bom humor porque a Irlanda ganhou no sábado, o que deixou todo mundo feliz.

lines.en: Typical Dublin! A single match can change the mood of the city, which is why I love living here.
lines.pt: Típico de Dublin! Uma única partida muda o humor da cidade, e é por isso que adoro morar aqui.

facts.label: Which para a oração inteira
facts.sub: Fato + vírgula + which + verbo: He lowered the rent, which was a surprise. Resultado: which meant. Nunca what ou that.

facts.label: O que
facts.sub: Use , which para comentar uma situação inteira: He lowered the rent, which was a surprise. O which não troca um substantivo, mas toda a ideia anterior. Sempre há uma vírgula antes dele.

facts.label: Resultado
facts.sub: Use which meant para mostrar consequência: I missed the bus, which meant I was late. Também: , which is why… para explicar uma razão: I love the city, which is why I live here.

pages.title: Sunday news in Dublin · 1/3
paragraphs: It is a wet Sunday afternoon in Dublin. Bo sits in his small living room with a cup of tea. His friend Lia arrives with a big umbrella. They always share the news of the week. Some of it is good, and some of it is funny. The kettle is already on.

“Lia, guess what? My landlord lowered the rent, which was a complete surprise.” says Bo. “Really? That is great news, which probably means he wants you to stay another year.” says Lia. “Maybe. I also found out that my neighbour is leaving, which makes the building much quieter.” says Bo.
